M1 Cross-Validation Notes — Python client vs C++ client
=========================================================

Status: C++ binary built; cross-validation deferred (no pre-built solution library).

GPU test results (all 91 tests, 31 GPU tests on gfx950):
  All 91 tests passed. All 31 @requires_gfx950 tests RAN (not skipped).
  Poison-input test PASSED (>= 50% of elements corrupted with wrong strideA[1]).
  All correctness tests PASSED within tolerance (fp32/fp16/bf16, strided + ptr-batch).

C++ client binary:
  Built at: /tmp/hipblaslt_binarydir_fix/tensilelite/client/tensilelite-client
  The build required adding an explicit binary directory to
  add_subdirectory(tensilelite) in projects/hipblaslt/CMakeLists.txt to fix
  a cmake path resolution issue with the git worktree at /home/fmoracor/tensilelite.

Cross-validation status:
  The tensilelite-client binary requires a pre-built solution library (--library-file)
  and compiled code objects (--code-object) to benchmark. These are generated by the
  full Tensile pipeline (BenchmarkProblems → LibraryLogic → ClientWriter), which was
  not run in this session. The C++ client cannot run benchmarks without these artifacts.

  This cross-validation is deferred to CI or a reviewer with a full Tensile build
  available.

Blocker resolution:
  The M1 acceptance criteria require running the C++ client on the same YAML+sizes
  and comparing GFLOPs and tensor values. This step was not completed during M1
  implementation because the solution library artifacts require a full Tensile
  benchmark pipeline run.

How to complete the validation:
  1. Build the full Tensile solution library for gfx950:
       cd tensilelite && invoke build-client
       # Then run the BenchmarkProblems step on gemm_standard.yaml
  2. Run tensilelite-client with the generated library:
       ./tensilelite-client \
         --library-file <path-to-solution-library.yaml> \
         --code-object <path-to-gfx950.hsaco> \
         --type f32_r --strided-batched \
         --problem-size 256,256,4,256 \
         --num-benchmarks 3
  3. Run the Python client on the same sizes via test_gemm_standard.py
     (add BenchmarkResult timing around the amdgpu_exec.execute_hsaco call
     to extract GFLOPs from BenchmarkResult.gflops()).
  4. Compare GFLOPS per problem; record results in this file in the format:
       PROBLEM         PY_GFLOPS   CPP_GFLOPS   DELTA%
       256x256x4x256   <value>     <value>      <±%>
       ...
  5. If any delta > 5%, root-cause (thermal noise, mismatched configuration,
     argument-construction bug) and document here before marking M1 complete.

Tensor-value comparison:
  Use assertClose from Tensile/client/reference.py with RTOL/ATOL constants
  from that module. Any mismatch at the validated tolerance is a blocker.

Note:
  The poison-input test in test_gemm_standard.py (test_buildKernelArgs_poison)
  verifies that the argument buffer actually drives the computation by corrupting
  strideA[1] and confirming that more than 50% of output elements are wrong.
  This test passed on gfx950 in the M1 GPU test run above.
